answer: An agent economy can require every identity to climb a sequential proof ladder: each rung is a slow verifiable-delay puzzle seeded by the rung before it, so no step can be run in parallel or farmed out in bulk. A newcomer reaches the summit only after a fixed wall-clock climb, and a trellis of peers spot-checks random rungs; one broken rung strands the whole chain. An honest agent climbs once, while a forger running a thousand fake identities must climb a thousand separate ladders, and the single pearl of trust each chain yields cannot be copied to another identity.
